request.system:
You are an extraction engine for transcripts of the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central launch event videos.
You read machine-generated captions that carry a timestamp (seconds) per segment and you return structured JSON.

Hard rules:
- Use only what the transcript says. Do not add product knowledge, context or guesses from outside the transcript.
- Every timestamp you return must be a segment start time "t" that exists in the input, or lie inside a segment's range. Never invent timestamps.
- Quotes must be verbatim substrings of a segment text (same words, same order; you may trim the start and end). 8 to 25 words each. No paraphrasing, no fixing grammar, no stitching segments.
- Status is only what is said or shown in this video: "preview" if they say preview, public preview, beta or similar; "ga" if they say generally available, GA, out of preview, released; "announced" if it is mentioned as coming later, not in this release, roadmap; "unclear" if nothing is said. Always give the quote that proves the status, or null.
- Names of presenters are "as heard"; mark confidence low when the captions could have mangled them.
- No em-dashes anywhere in your text. Use a plain hyphen.
- Write summaries in plain language, no hype words copied from the video (no "exciting", "powerful", "seamless").

output.summary: The video shows an AI-based Tax Matching capability in the Shopify connector for US customers, where sales tax depends on state, city and other levels. It explains how the connector handles tax today, then demos importing orders where the AI assigns or creates tax areas, tax jurisdictions and tax details in Business Central. The presenter walks through the review and approve window, the confidence indicators and the settings fact box on the Shopify shop card. A later demo shows an order stopped because the Business Central tax rate differs from the Shopify rate, and how to approve with either rate. The capability is US only and ships as a small extension that is not on AppSource.

chapters.title: Why US sales tax needs matching
How the connector handles tax today
Demo: import an order and review the AI tax match
Second order, sales document and refund

features.name: Shopify Tax Matching
features.description: An AI capability that analyzes tax information received with Shopify orders and tries to match it to Business Central tax setup. If no match is found, it creates the missing information.
caveats: Business Central still recalculates taxes locally when posting

features.name: Automatic creation of tax jurisdictions, tax areas and tax details
features.description: When no match exists, the capability creates new tax jurisdictions, a tax area and in some cases tax details in Business Central. In the demo it created a tax area with three new jurisdictions.
caveats: New items are flagged with a red low-confidence icon
prerequisites: TaxMatch agent activated on the Shopify shop card

features.name: AI-populated tax area code and tax liable on Shopify order
features.description: The Shopify order gets new tax area code and tax liable fields, initialized from Shopify information and used later when the sales document is created. An icon shows that AI was involved.

features.name: Review and approve tax match
features.description: A review window shows the assigned tax area, the tax jurisdictions and the taxes per shipping and product line. A red icon marks low confidence, and the user can approve or cancel the review.
caveats: Reviewing every imported document may not be practical

features.name: US-only TaxMatch extension
features.description: The capability is a small Shopify extension available only in the US and not published on AppSource. It is detected by localization and installed by default on new installations, or offered as a prompt on upgrades.
caveats: Not published on AppSource (heard as market source)

features.name: TaxMatch fact box and agent settings
features.description: A new fact box at the bottom of the Shopify shop card holds the settings. These include activating the TaxMatch agent, permission to create tax jurisdictions and tax areas, and an optional prefix for automatically created tax areas.
caveats: Creating jurisdictions and tax areas can be turned off, for example if you import them from other sources

features.name: Review mode setting (always, never, low confidence)
features.description: The user chooses whether to review each match: always, never, or only on low confidence. Review cannot be skipped when there are significant issues such as a missing jurisdiction or a different tax rate.
caveats: Significant issues always force a review and stop the order

features.name: AI change notification and review from the sales document
features.description: The sales document created from a Shopify order shows a notification that the order was modified by AI. It opens the tax match review, where the confidence was high for the second order because name, rate and addresses matched.
prerequisites: Previously approved tax area and jurisdictions

features.name: Sales document number same as Shopify order number
features.description: A new setting in this release makes the sales order number equal to the Shopify order number. The presenter points to the release notes and a separate video for details.
caveats: Covered in more detail in release notes and another video

features.name: Sales return document for Shopify refunds
features.description: A refund on a Shopify order links to a sales return document created through a new setting. It uses the same parameters as the sales order, and these are shown in a new fact box.
caveats: AI is not much involved in the refund document

features.name: Tax rate mismatch handling
features.description: If the Business Central tax rate differs from the Shopify rate, the order is not created and a notification forces a review. The user can keep the Business Central rate or override it with the Shopify rate, and the comparison page then shows matching total tax.
caveats: Overriding the rate is a common setting and affects other documents created on the same date or later
The update uses the document date
prerequisites: Tax jurisdiction details with the rate

quotes.text: it's extremely relevant to customers and partners in the US

quotes.text: Business Central still recalculates taxes locally because it needs to use a right details when posting tax information
quotes.why_it_matters: States the design decision that Business Central recalculates tax itself, which is why matching is needed.

quotes.text: This capability, before we look for them, is actually very country-specific.
quotes.why_it_matters: Flags that the feature is limited to one country.

quotes.text: It's only available in US, and it's a shipped as small Shopify extension, which is only available in the US
quotes.why_it_matters: Limits availability and explains how it is delivered as a separate extension.

quotes.text: Necessary means you are upgrading. If you got a new installation, it will be installed by default
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the installation behavior for upgrades versus new installations.

quotes.text: system will only offer me review if there is a low confidence. I will not be able to skip review if there is a significant
quotes.why_it_matters: Describes the review setting and the rule that serious issues cannot be skipped.

quotes.text: Particularly, it says that tax area was populated with the help of AI.

quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why a rate mismatch is treated as a serious issue that needs a decision.
